Dear Tarek,

I'm not sure this has to do with irace. It seems an error message given by another package (doSnow?): https://github.com/tobigithub/R-parallel/wiki/R-parallel-Errors#error-error-in-summaryconnectionconnection--invalid-connection

I see that you got the error also at the top of your screenshot before running.

1. Try launching irace from a fresh R console without running anything else before it.

2. Do not launch any parallel stuff or load any parallel libraries before launching irace. If you want irace to run in parallel, you have to use the options provided by irace, otherwise, it will not work.

Let us know if any of the above fixes the issue so that we can add it to the FAQ.

Best wishes,

Manuel.

Could you run without parallel? That is, set parallel=0. It seems that the debug output is not shown in Windows when running in parallel (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56501937/how-to-print-from-clusterapply). Without the debug output, I don't know if irace is waiting for your algorithm to finish running or there is a bug in irace. I don't have Windows and this works fine in Linux.

You don't need to run also the recovery.

Cheers,

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Re: problem in recovery
parts:
Dear Tarek,

We don't have an option (yet) to terminate the target-algorithm after a number
of seconds. There is now a timeout option that we could use:

https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/system2.html

but it only works in recent versions of R (>= 3.5). I'm also not sure what
irace should do after such a timeout occurs. Should irace stop with an error?
If not, should it consider the configuration that failed to be an immediate
rejection (see the User guide to read about immediate rejection) or should it
assign a penalty value?

Looking at your screenshot, Java is the one taking 32% of the CPU, while R is
not consuming any cpu, which suggests that irace is waiting for your algorithm
to finish. There must be some way in Java to set a timeout.

I have also tried to access your link but it says "Access denied". In any case,
it may be useful to make your algorithm print some progress to a temporary
output file so that you can check that irace is the one frozen and not your
algorithm.


Cheers,

Manuel.
